To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sensitivity and specificity in detecting the Leishmania infection in buffy coat and in saliva, among Thai patients with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in Trang Province, were 73.8% and 100%, and 26.1 and 100%, accordingly.
the nested-PCR to detect Leishmaniain saliva is less sensitive than buffy coat for the diagnosis of asymptomatic VL infection in patients with HIV/AIDS.
Leishmania DNA was detected in 12.1%, 73.9%, and 26.1%, of patients with HIV/AIDS using buffy coat, saliva, and both buffy coat plus saliva, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of Leishmania in saliva and buffy coats among Thai patients with asymptomatic VL.
the detection of Leishmania in saliva among patients infected with HIV/AIDS.
the use of saliva as a non-invasive specimen for detecting asymptomatic Leishmanias infection in Thai patients with HIV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nested-PCR to detect Leishmaniain saliva is not a good alternative for the diagnosis of Leishmania in patients with HIV/AIDS.
the nested-PCR to detect Leishmanias in buffy coat and/or saliva is useful for diagnosis of asymptomatic Leishmanias among HIV-infected individuals.
the nested-PCR to detect Leishmanias DNA in saliva is a useful tool for screening Leishmania infection, but it is not a diagnostic method for VL among patients with HIV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
saliva is an alternative specimen for Leishmania diagnosis among patients with HIV, but buffy coat remains the best specimen.
buffy coat is a better specimen for diagnosing Leishmania infection than saliva.
saliva is not recommended for Leishmania diagnosis in patients with HIV/AIDS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nested-PCR can detect the presence of Leishmania in saliva.
the use of saliva as a specimen to diagnose VL in HIV-infected individuals is a noninvasive method and requires less expertise.
saliva is an alternative specimen for the diagnosis of asymptomatic Leishmanias infection among patients with AIDS.
